react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: disrupted androgen and estrogen steroidogenesis. RaMP multi-DB over-representation analysis (FDR 2.93e-15) identified 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) with five steroid hits out of seven input metabolites, yielding a fold-enrichment of 1667.9. The same pathway ranked first in Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p=0.000252, 11 of 11 matched network nodes, 100% pathway coverage), confirming that the mass-spectral signal is not an annotation artefact. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-based PSEA confirmed the same pathway at p=2.5e-06 with five hits, providing a third independent statistical vote. Reactome 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (R-HSA-196071, FDR 1.67e-14) and WikiPathways 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496, FDR 2.78e-13) extend the signal to broader steroid biochemistry, all sharing the same five driver steroids. Guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581) independently maps to glycine/serine metabolism and the urea cycle with borderline significance (MetaboAnalystR p=0.118), consistent with its role as the direct arginine-glycerol precursor to creatine. N-Acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) maps to amino-sugar and hyaluronan metabolism via Mummichog (p=0.049). The five steroid drivers — estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone — are all confirmed members of the KEGG:hsa00140, SMPDB:SMP00068, and REACT:R-HSA-196071 rosters. The cross-paradigm consensus of a single dominant pathway with five matched driver metabolites constitutes strong evidence for systemic perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion in the treatment group.

  "narrative_text": "RaMP multi-DB over-representation analysis identified 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00356) as the top pathway with FDR of 2.93e-15, driven by five steroid metabolites: estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone). final_react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-DB over-representation analysis identified 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00356) as the top pathway with FDR of 2.93e-15, driven by five steroid metabolites: estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone). The second-ranked pathway Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068) shares the same five driver steroids and identical FDR of 2.93e-15. KEGG:map00150 Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism also appears as rank 3 with identical enrichment statistics, confirming cross-database consistency. Reactome R-HSA-196071 Metabolism of steroid hormones extends the signal to a broader pathway context with FDR of 1.67e-14. The five steroids map consistently across these three pathway databases, with fold-enrichment of 1667.9 and 1154.7 respectively. N-Acetylgalactosamine (C01074) and guanidoacetic acid (C00581) did not reach significance in the steroid hormone pathways, suggesting selective perturbation of androgen and estrogen interconversion rather than global metabolic disruption.
